title: Upvote and the vote model: one per person per item, materialised tallies
description:
As a signed-in reader, I want to upvote an item, so that good items rise.

Vote model: subject, voter, voterRole (editor or reader, set at write time), kind (up or rating), dimension, value, timestamp; one per person per subject and kind. Tallies are materialised, not computed on read. Built as a Papyrus plugin using the existing plugin contract (manifest, signed-in mutation, WAF rules).

```gherkin
Feature: Upvote
  Scenario: Cast
    Given a signed-in reader and an item
    When the reader upvotes
    Then exactly one upvote exists for that reader and item
    And the upvote tally increases by one

  Scenario: Repeat
    When the reader upvotes again
    Then nothing changes (idempotent) or the vote is withdrawn, per the documented rule

  Scenario: Guest
    When a guest tries to vote
    Then the request is rejected

  Scenario: Role recorded
    When an editor votes
    Then the vote carries voterRole "editor" and is tallied separately
```

comments.author: home
comments.text: Reconciliation 2026-10-22. Mostly done, kept open for one gap. Exists: vote model with voterRole (editor or reader, set at write time), one vote per reader and item, idempotent upvote and removal via POST /api/reader/vote, guests rejected, only published items votable (Papyrus #512, amplify/plugins/reader-steering/function/handler.py, schema.ts); materialised public counts via the reader snapshot, _data/reader/items.json (#516, debounce #520). Remains: the upvote count in the snapshot ('up') mixes editors and readers; the scenario 'editor votes are tallied separately' needs a separate editor upvote tally.
